purpose: Eszopiclone is used to help you fall asleep and stay asleep if you have insomnia. It is meant for adults who have trouble sleeping. Your doctor may prescribe it for short-term or longer-term use depending on your situation.
how_it_works: Your brain has natural calming chemicals, and this medicine helps boost their effect to make you feel sleepy. Think of it like turning down the volume on the busy, awake parts of your brain so you can relax and drift off. It works pretty quickly, usually within 30 minutes of taking it.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is an unpleasant bitter or metallic taste in your mouth the next morning. You may also feel drowsy, dizzy, or have a headache the next day. Some people notice dry mouth or feel a little anxious.
warnings: Do not drive or do anything that requires full alertness the morning after taking this medicine, as it can still make you drowsy. Avoid alcohol while taking Eszopiclone because it can make the sleepiness dangerously worse. In rare cases, some people do unusual things while asleep, like sleepwalking or sleep-driving, without remembering it — tell your doctor right away if this happens. This medicine can be habit-forming, so only take it exactly as prescribed.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 1 mg taken right before bedtime. Your doctor may increase it to 2 mg or 3 mg if needed. Only take it when you have at least 7 to 8 hours available to sleep before you need to be awake and active.
